SEC11A-01.note: Boundary item: participial phrase must open the new sentence to modify 'the geologists'. C/D comma splices; B dangles the participle onto the first clause. Key is the only period option (odd one out). PHASE 2: Key and explanation agree with my cold reasoning.

SEC11A-02.note: Long subject; the nonrestrictive 'which' clause opened with a comma must close with one before main verb 'shows'. A folds 'shows' into the relative clause (no main verb); C fragment; D dash mismatches comma. PHASE 2: Agrees; explanation correct.

SEC11A-03.note: Second clause has a noun-clause subject ('that the two ... descend') with verb 'was not demonstrated'; only the semicolon separates the clauses. A reads as a relative clause and strands 'was'; B splice; D removes the subject. PHASE 2: Agrees; explanation correctly names the noun-clause subject.

SEC11A-04.note: 'its oak hull ... had begun' is independent; period required. A splice, B run-on, C 'with' strands 'had begun'. Key again the lone period option. PHASE 2: Agrees; the absolute-phrase lure in A is the best distractor.

SEC11A-05.note: 'only after ... did the astronomers' is an inverted independent clause; needs ', and'. A splice, B run-on, D 'even after' cannot license the inversion and changes the sense (strikable). PHASE 2: Agrees; explanation of the inversion is correct.

SEC11A-06.note: Two independent clauses; semicolon. A splice, B run-on, C 'alongside' removes the subject of 'suggest'. PHASE 2: Agrees; explanation correct.

SEC11B-01.note: Postponed direct object of 'singled out' after an 'as' phrase; no punctuation between the complement phrase and the object. B single comma separates verb from object; C colon after a non-independent clause; D 'was' is ungrammatical (strikable). PHASE 2: Agrees; explanation correct.

SEC11B-02.note: Subject 'sonatas' + restrictive 'that' clause, then main verb 'circulated': no punctuation. The inner comma pair invites a comma after 'pupils' (A). C makes 'circulated' part of the relative clause; D dash unpaired. PHASE 2: Agrees; explanation correct.

SEC11B-03.note: Second sentence part is 'because the quarry ..., the building's stories were finished', needing a coordinator: ', but because'. A and B leave a splice (B with 'however'); D 'but the quarry flooded' leaves 'the building's ... were finished' spliced on. PHASE 2: Agrees; explanation correct.

SEC11B-04.note: Comma after 'demonstrated' opens the 'using ...' interrupter, so a comma must close it before the object clause 'that the total mass ...'. Counter-intuitive comma before 'that'; A dash tempting because dashes appear inside the interrupter but mismatches the opening comma; B no close; C semicolon. PHASE 2: Agrees; explanation correct.

SEC11B-05.note: Two independent clauses; semicolon. B splice, C run-on, D ', however,' still a splice. PHASE 2: Agrees. Minor: explanation lumps 'return among the' (no comma) under 'comma splice'; it is a fused sentence. Reasoning still supports the key.

SEC11B-06.note: Garden path: introductory 'Because' clause ends at 'study'; comma before main-clause subject 'Latin and Greek ... were offered'. A makes them the object and strands 'were offered'; C/D colon/semicolon after a dependent clause. PHASE 2: Agrees; explanation correct.
